lines.trans: Excuse me, have you seen my wallet?
That means it was stolen on the metro.
All of my money was in there.
It is a good thing my passport was in another pocket.
After all, you cannot pay at a hotel with a ticket.
Fine, we will lend him a little money.
Nastya, bring our secret cash stash here.
I ordered a children's wardrobe with it.
We were going to buy a new television!

words.gloss: to intend, to be about to; to gather

lines.trans: You cannot put children's clothes inside a television.
Start mending your relationship at last.
And I will go order that wardrobe.

examples.text: Начинайте наконец налаживать ваши отношения.
examples.trans: Start mending your relationship at last.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и налаживать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and to mend on time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Начинайте наконец налаживать ваши отношения.
examples.trans: Start mending your relationship at last.

examples.text: Там вашей маме стало очень плохо.
examples.trans: Your mother has been taken very ill over there.

examples.text: Скажите, это ваш гостиничный номер?
examples.trans: Tell me, is this your hotel room?

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'ношение'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'relationship' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Начинайте наконец налаживать ваши отношения.
examples.trans: Start mending your relationship at last.

examples.text: А я испорчу отношения с будущим мэром.
examples.trans: And I'll ruin my relationship with the future mayor.

examples.text: У нас очень тёплые отношения.
examples.trans: We have a very warm relationship.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Тебе ещё не надоела серая Москва?
examples.trans: Are you not tired of gray Moscow yet?

examples.text: Может, поедешь со мной в Париж?
examples.trans: Maybe you will go to Paris with me?

examples.text: Там мы найдём тебе хорошую работу.
examples.trans: There we will find you a good job.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will go', paired with 'идти'.

examples.text: Пойдём быстрее на свежий воздух.
examples.trans: Let us go quickly to the fresh air.

examples.text: А я пойду закажу этот шкаф.
examples.trans: And I will go order that wardrobe.

examples.text: Пойдём скорее отсюда, мой дорогой.
examples.trans: Let us go quickly from here, my dear.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Слышишь, это сработала пожарная сигнализация.
examples.trans: Listen, the fire alarm has gone off.

examples.text: Ничего страшного, это просто красное вино.
examples.trans: No big deal, it is just red wine.

examples.text: Что это за внеплановый семейный совет?
examples.trans: What is this unscheduled family council?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Ладно, проходите уже в комнату.
examples.trans: Fine, go on into the room already.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Come in, please.

examples.text: Проходи на кухню.
examples.trans: Come through to the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: По-моему, я уже жутко опаздываю.
examples.trans: In my opinion, I am already terribly late.

examples.text: Он уже позвал тебя замуж?
examples.trans: Has he already asked you to marry him?

examples.text: Она у нас уже взрослый человек.
examples.trans: She is already a grown adult.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'room' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Ладно, проходите уже в комнату.
examples.trans: Fine, go on into the room already.

examples.text: Скажите, в комнате уже всё готово?
examples.trans: Tell me, is everything ready in the room already?

examples.text: Где ваша комната?
examples.trans: Where is your room?
